tldr: Evening batch (Sep 18): the day's security stories were about what agents can already reach. Air Security's Plugin4Shell showed a zero-click RCE in four coding agents - Anthropic patched Claude Code, OpenAI patched Codex, Copilot has no fix, and Google will not patch the Gemini CLI it is retiring - because the agents fetch a plugin's pinned commit snapshot without ever checking that the code they install matches it, so a repository owner needs only a git host that allows hash-shaped branch names, such as Bitbucket. Separately, Hacktron chained a heap overflow and an SSO misconfiguration through an OpenAI staff forum to reach internal repositories, using Claude to help write the exploit, and Zhipu's ZCode was caught shipping entire workspaces and .git history to Aliyun OSS under a server-supplied key. Math and risk collided on the same day: 42 Royal Society fellows, Fields medallists among them, told their academy that AI existential risk is real and urgent, while Timothy Gowers published why he would not sign it, and US and China experts put shared human-control red lines over nuclear weapons on the table a week before Trump and Xi meet. Money kept concentrating - Crusoe raised $3.9B for data centers and modular 'AI factories' at a $30.9B valuation, Mantic raised $25M after its agents beat humans at forecasting, and Google stood up the DeepMind Institute and its economic-policy-for-AGI essay to widen a debate it also sits inside. Unredacted court exhibits in The Times v. OpenAI showed a Microsoft executive calling the training-data pipeline the largest theft of labor in human history. On the open side, a teardown found Ternary Bonsai 2's own documents fall short of its 98.2% claim, OpenJev put typed-option logits in a browser on WebGPU, a component-level study isolated context management as the harness variable that matters most when the window tightens, and a US government site was found running a Qwen-based search tool the FBI has said copied Anthropic.

articles.title: Microsoft exec called AI scraping 'the largest theft of labor in human history'
articles.summary: Unredacted exhibits in The Times v. OpenAI and Microsoft: a top Microsoft executive privately called the training-data pipeline 'theft'.

articles.title: Plugin4Shell: a zero-click RCE across four AI coding agents
articles.summary: A plugin's repo owner can point a hash-named branch at different code. Claude Code 2.1.179 and Codex 0.146.0 patched; Copilot unfixed. Needs a non-GitHub host.

articles.title: OpenAI 'ethically hacked' with the help of Anthropic's Claude
articles.summary: Hacktron reached OpenAI staff ChatGPT accounts and internal repos via a forum and an SSO misconfiguration. 'The scope of what we could access was huge.'

articles.title: ZCode was silently uploading whole workspaces, .git history included
articles.summary: Zhipu's coding app packaged repos, LFS cache, reflogs and global configs, encrypted them with a server-supplied key and shipped it to Aliyun OSS.

articles.title: 42 Royal Society fellows tell their academy AI risk is real and urgent
articles.summary: Fields medallists Martin Hairer and Peter Scholze among the signatories, who say the labs' own above-10% x-risk estimates must not be dismissed as hype.

articles.title: Why Timothy Gowers did not sign the Fields medallists' letter
articles.summary: The Fields medallist agrees there is a crisis but disputes the framing, and says he worries more about a lost generation of PhD mathematicians.

articles.title: US and China experts push shared red lines on AI and nuclear weapons
articles.summary: Brookings' Melanie Sisson and Fudan's Tianjiao Jiang want AI barred from launch decisions and a common definition of human control. Trump and Xi meet Sept 24.

articles.title: A US government website ran a Qwen-based search tool the FBI said copied Anthropic
articles.summary: Reuters finds a US government site running Chinese AI search infrastructure on a product the FBI has flagged as copied from Anthropic.

articles.title: Crusoe raises $3.9B to build data centers and modular 'AI factories'
articles.summary: A $3.9B Series F at a $30.9B post-money for OpenAI's Stargate partner, split between large campuses and small modular 'AI factories'.

articles.title: Google DeepMind stands up an institute to widen the AGI debate
articles.summary: Its stated aim is to surface disagreement inside Google DeepMind and with outside researchers: 'They will not always agree.'

articles.title: DeepMind's institute publishes an economic policy for AGI
articles.summary: The first substantive output of the new institute: what economic policy looks like if AGI arrives, in the lab's own framing.

articles.title: The UN turns to Google to make its global data agent-ready
articles.summary: Google is helping the UN restructure public data so agents, not humans, can consume it - machine-readability as the new access layer.

articles.title: The FAA's plan to fix air traffic: $875M worth of AI
articles.summary: The agency is leaning on roughly $875 million of AI to shore up air traffic control, per TechCrunch.

articles.title: Waymo is coming to Singapore, with rides targeted for 2028
articles.summary: Mapping drives with its 5th-gen Driver and Jaguar I-PACE start next year; LTA approval is sought in 2027, commercial service in 2028.

articles.title: OpenJev runs typed option logits locally in a browser on WebGPU
articles.summary: An open reimplementation of TypeSafe's Jev: read option probabilities and autoregressive JSON from open models on your own machine, no round trip.

articles.title: Ternary Bonsai 2's own documents undercut its 98.2% claim
articles.summary: The model's own docs show 52.8 and 60.8 against Qwen3.5-27B's 69.7 and 80.6 - roughly three quarters retained, not near-lossless.

articles.title: Flyweight: an open C++/CUDA engine for MoE models bigger than your VRAM
articles.summary: Native GGUF runtime with OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs, one consumer GPU plus system RAM. First PyPI release, looking for contributors.

articles.title: An empirical study of harness design for coding agents
articles.summary: 176 matched settings across four models: context management pays off fastest as the window tightens, mostly by preventing overflow failures.

articles.title: Mantic raises $25M after its agents beat human forecasters
articles.summary: Radical Ventures led, with Microsoft's M12 and Thinking Machines Lab. Its system beat every human entrant in the summer 2026 Metaculus Cup.

articles.title: Qwen 3.8 27B squeezed into 13.1GB of VRAM
articles.summary: Shapelearn's write-up on fitting a 27B Qwen into 13.1GB - the local-model footprint curve keeps falling under consumer hardware.

articles.title: Huawei plans a new AI chip for Q1 2027 as it takes on Nvidia
articles.summary: Huawei sets a Q1 2027 launch window for its next AI accelerator, per TechCrunch, as domestic demand outruns supply.
